questions.prompt: Why does Chapter 2 put lovable project next to one skill at a time?
choices: Because emotional pull and narrow scope both protect the learner's return to practice
Because the chapter wants learners to sample many small hobbies at once
Because motivation matters only after the skill is mostly mastered

explanation.gentle: The project has to matter enough to revisit, but it also has to stay small enough for repetition to compound.
explanation.direct: The pair works together: interest keeps the loop alive, and scope control keeps the loop from fragmenting.
explanation.competitive: Desire gets you back. Narrowing stops the session from leaking everywhere.

questions.prompt: What job does target performance level do in the chapter's method?
choices: It gives the learner a visible threshold that tells practice what to serve
It replaces the need for deconstruction and feedback
It proves that long sessions are no longer necessary

explanation.gentle: A clear performance line shows what usable success would look like and helps the learner choose what to practice first.
explanation.direct: The target level creates selection pressure. It turns a broad dream into a nearer functional standard.
explanation.competitive: Without the line, every subskill keeps stealing time.

questions.prompt: Which move best reflects the chapter's view of deconstruction?
choices: Breaking the skill into parts so the most important parts can receive early reps
Studying every subskill equally to avoid blind spots
Delaying practice until the full map of the skill is complete

explanation.gentle: The chapter values deconstruction because it helps the learner isolate what matters now.
explanation.direct: Breaking the skill down is useful only when it directs repetition toward the critical few elements.
explanation.competitive: Deconstruction earns its keep when it creates sharper reps, not larger diagrams.

questions.prompt: Priya keeps practicing her entire robotics competition at once and leaves each session scattered. What response best fits Chapter 2?
choices: Keep broad practice for motivation and trust that repetition will sort it out later
Choose one visible subskill and repeat it against a clear threshold tonight
Pause practice until the team agrees on the perfect season-long training plan

explanation.gentle: The chapter would narrow the target so repetition can finally compound on one trainable piece.
explanation.direct: One-skill focus plus a visible performance line is the right correction to scattered effort.
explanation.competitive: She needs one rep lane, not a bigger fantasy.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest reason the chapter cares about barriers to practice?
choices: They determine how often the learner actually reaches the first rep
They prove whether the learner truly wants the skill badly enough
They make it easier to justify buying better tools

explanation.gentle: Small bits of friction often decide whether practice happens at all.
explanation.direct: Barrier removal matters because entry cost controls return frequency.
explanation.competitive: Setup friction is one of the quietest ways to starve a project.

questions.prompt: The chapter warns that speed can backfire. When does that happen?
choices: When the learner moves quickly enough to stay emotionally engaged
When faster cycles happen without useful feedback to correct the next attempt
When the learner uses short sessions instead of long sessions

explanation.gentle: Faster reps help only when the learner gets enough signal to improve the next one.
explanation.direct: Speed without correction can automate error instead of building competence.
explanation.competitive: Fast mistakes are still mistakes if the loop never teaches.

questions.prompt: Luis thinks only two-hour weekend coding blocks will move him forward. Chapter 2 would most likely say what?
choices: Shorter weekday bursts are stronger if they produce more corrected attempts
Weekend marathons are always superior because they feel more serious
He should stop coding until he has more uninterrupted time

explanation.gentle: The chapter values session design by what increases return frequency and useful feedback, not by what looks impressive.
explanation.direct: If shorter bursts create denser, feedback-rich reps, they are the better loop.
explanation.competitive: Heroic duration loses to repeatable correction.

questions.prompt: Owen keeps improving his guitar setup but rarely plays. Which diagnosis best fits the chapter?
choices: He is wisely building motivation through better tools
He has confused barrier removal with readiness theater and is not shortening the path to the next rep
He should add more planning so the setup becomes fully optimized

explanation.gentle: The chapter supports preparation only when it makes practice easier to begin right away.
explanation.direct: Useful setup lowers entry cost. Owen's behavior is drifting into preparation that feels serious without increasing contact.
explanation.competitive: His discipline costume is hiding empty hands.

questions.prompt: When does a clean practice system become setup theater according to the chapter's hardest warning?
choices: When the learner uses timers, checklists, and tools to support real repetition
When the structure looks organized but does not increase dense, informed attempts at the right subskill
When the learner focuses on one skill instead of many

explanation.gentle: The chapter's real test is not whether the system looks good. It is whether the loop is producing more useful contact with the skill.
explanation.direct: Preparation crosses into theater when it improves the appearance of seriousness without tightening the rep-and-feedback loop.
explanation.competitive: If the reps stay thin, the machine is fake.

questions.prompt: If Chapter 2 explains how to tighten the rep loop, what is the most natural next question for Chapter 3?
choices: How much pre-practice learning helps the loop before it turns into delay?
How can a learner remove all frustration from practice?
How can a learner skip deconstruction and go straight to speed?

explanation.gentle: Once the loop is designed, the reader still needs to know how much study strengthens it without replacing action.
explanation.direct: Chapter 2 raises the preparation boundary problem. Chapter 3 logically asks where useful learning ends and research mode begins.
explanation.competitive: The next fight is against elegant delay, not against structure.
